key_insight: AI agents improved quantum compilation constructions through iterative program optimization, with every result certified by a frozen, exact verifier.
engineering_relevance: Lower-cost fermion-to-qubit encodings, Hamiltonian layouts and unitary synthesis could help quantum algorithms run more efficiently on real devices.
method: An agent formulates the optimization challenge with a researcher and builds an exact verifier.
Validate the verifier against a solved case, deliberately broken solutions and published results, then freeze it.
Agents iteratively improve programs against a fixed evaluator, recording notes that later agents can build on.
evidence_signal: Across three quantum compilation problems, agents reduced the optimized cost by up to 73% at the largest sizes tested and outperformed a state-of-the-art fermion-to-qubit encoding optimizer.
watch_item: The approach requires exact, efficient verification; the reported cost reductions do not by themselves establish hardware-level performance gains.
paper_title: Automating quantum circuit optimization with AI agents
